name: Death-related Mental Imagery — 8-item research measure
original_measure: Holmes et al. suicide-related mental imagery checklist / Scottish Wellbeing Study 8-item implementation
construct: Frequency of suicide/death-related mental imagery when distressed
version: 8-item Scottish Wellbeing Study-style fixed subset derived from Holmes et al. (2007)
response_model: 8 items; 0=None of the time to 4=All of the time; sum 0–32
rights: Holmes et al. (2007) is open access under CC BY 3.0. The De Beurs et al. (2019) source paper is CC BY 4.0 and describes an 8-item death-related imagery measure based on Holmes et al. The eight categories here correspond to the fixed checklist categories used in that research lineage, excluding the open-ended 'any other type' category.
license: CC BY 3.0 / CC BY 4.0 source lineage
safety: This measure must not be interpreted as an individual suicide-risk probability. Endorsement of current imagery involving planning/preparing self-harm or a suicide attempt should trigger direct human assessment under the study-approved safety protocol.

items.text: Images of a time when you tried to harm yourself in the past
Images of yourself planning/preparing to harm yourself or make a suicide attempt
Images of what might happen to you if you died
Images of what might happen to other people if you died
Images of things you were escaping from
Images of another distressing event that happened to you, for example a trauma
Images that made you feel safe or better
Images that were fleeting or unclear
